title: How to Compare Process Management Tools Before You Choose
summary: Compare process management tools with objective criteria for automation, integration, and customization before you choose.
body_markdown:
To **compare process management tools** , the most important criterion isn't the feature list, it's the level of automation, integration, and customization your operation actually needs. Tools like Notion, Airtable, ClickUp, Pipefy, Monday, and **Jestor** come up in these searches, and the right choice depends on which of these factors matters most for your process.


The question usually comes up after a company has already tried a tool and felt something was missing: more automation, tighter integration with finance, or more freedom to move beyond a fixed board-and-card model.


Comparing tools with clear criteria helps avoid switching again a few months later, for the same reason.


## What Usually Weighs on the Comparison


- Whether the process fits entirely into a simple Kanban model, or needs forms, tables, and automations combined
- Whether the tool integrates natively with the ERP the company already uses, without relying on Zapier or Make
- Whether automations can be built without code, directly by the operations team
- Whether granular permission control exists, by role, field, and action
- Whether the data stays exportable, without locking the company into the chosen tool


## How to Structure the Comparison, Step by Step


1. List the processes that need management (approvals, CRM, tasks, support), not just the most obvious one
2. Mark, for each tool considered, whether it covers these processes with real automation or just a visual board
3. Check integration with the ERP and with WhatsApp, two common friction points day to day
4. Test the learning curve with the team that will actually use it, not just the person deciding
5. Consider the total cost, including intermediaries like Zapier or Make, if they're needed


Criterion Why it matters


Native automation Reduces reliance on intermediary tools and extra cost


ERP integration Avoids manual entry and duplicate data work


Flexibility beyond Kanban Covers processes that don't fit into just a board and cards


Granular permissions Controls who edits each part of the process

## Frequently asked questions


**Is there one process management tool that fits every company?** Not exactly; the right choice depends on the level of automation and integration the specific process requires.


**Does Jestor replace simple Kanban tools?** It covers the same Kanban use case and adds automation and integration; see more at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Do I need several connected tools to cover every process?** Not necessarily, **Jestor** brings Kanban, forms, tables, and automations together in one place.


**Is it worth switching tools if the process already works, just slowly?** It's worth reevaluating once the time lost to manual work outweighs the cost of migrating.


To **compare process management tools** with objective criteria, not just the interface, is what keeps you from choosing again in six months.
